conflicts.message: Feature 'rt' is implied by 'rt-multi-thread'. It is redundant to enable both.
Feature 'signal' requires 'process' internally. Enabling 'signal' alone is sufficient.
TLS backends are mutually exclusive. Choose exactly one (native-tls, rustls-tls, or default-tls).
Both features pull in additional heavy dependencies. Consider if both are required.
Feature 'std' already implies 'alloc'. Enabling both explicitly is usually redundant.

bloat.message: Adds OpenSSL binding. If rustls is already used elsewhere, consider switching to 'rustls' feature to reduce duplicate TLS stacks.
Adds serde_json. If serde_json is already present via other dependencies, this feature may be unnecessary.
Adds mime and bytes crates. Use only if multipart uploads are needed.
Adds proc-macro dependency. Consider using manual Serialize/Deserialize impls for small crates.
Enables a broad async surface area. Prefer enabling only the Tokio sub-features your crate actually uses.

suggest_opt_out.reason: Default features pull in no dependencies but enable the 'std' feature. If you are using a no-std logger, set default-features = false.
Default features enable 'default-tls' (native-tls). Often rustls-tls is preferred in pure Rust environments.
Default features enable 'std'. For no-std crates that only need allocation support, set default-features = false and opt into 'alloc' explicitly.
